The Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) is a concept introduced under India's National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020). It is a novel and innovative system that aims to promote flexibility and transparency in higher education by enabling students to accumulate academic credits for the courses they complete. The ABC system is designed to facilitate seamless mobility and facilitate multiple entry and exit points for learners within the higher education framework.
Multiple Entry and Exit Points

The ABC system enables students to have multiple entry and exit points within the higher education system. This means that students can enroll, take a break, or exit the education system at different stages while still being able to retain the credits they have earned.

Prof. Deepanwita Srivastava Prof. Deepanwita Srivastava Designation: Professor Specialization: French, Tourism Studies Academic Level: 14 Joining: 01-02-2009 Brief Profile: Deepanwita Srivastava is Professor of French and specializes in the areas of Didactics of French Language, Open Distance & Distributed Learning, Translation & Interpretation and Travel & Mobility Studies. Alumna of the Centre of French and Francophone Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University, N.Delhi she has a long experience of teaching French at several universities and institutions of Higher Education and is counted among the pioneers of French Studies in Open Distance & Distributed Learning in India. Appointed Principal Lexicographer & Rédactrice en chef (Editor in Chief) for the United Nations Project on the Hindi-French Bilingual Dictionary with the Central Hindi Directorate-- CHD, Ministry of Education, Govt. of India. Designed and developed the first Master’s Program in French in India in the Open & Distance Learning Mode, created French language learning modules for SWAYAM MOOCs, and designed multiple curricula catering to Pedagogy of French as a Foreign Language–Français langue étrangère FLE in ODL models. Actively engaged with Language courses and Skill development in the FYUP Program under the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) (Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship - MSDE), Govt of India and the E-VBAB— E Vidya Bharati Project of the Govt. of India for students from Africa. Coordinator of the Ph.D program in French at the School of Foreign Languages, she has successfully guided several Doctoral research students at IGNOU as well as at other universities contributing to innovation and knowledge creation  in the domain of French Studies. Widely published and Invited/Visiting scholar at several universities abroad, she has been also recipient of International Fellowships from the Shastri Indo Canadian Institute - SICI, Asian Association of Open Universities - AAOU, UNESCO, and the ICSSR. Member, Advisory Boards, Comités scientifiques/Editorial Boards of International journals, Boards of Studies and Academic Councils of universities, Committees on Educational Policies, Curriculum Planning & Research Councils. Actively engaged in workshops, projects and collaborations with the French Embassy in India, Indian Council of Social Sciences Research (ICSSR, Ministry of Education, Govt. of India, Indian Council of Cultural Relations, Ministry of External Affairs, Govt. of India, UNESCO, Bureau du Quebec India,  CEMCA (Commonwealth of Learning- CoL Canada), the Shastri Indo Canadian Institute (SICI), India Africa Virtual University (IAVU, Ministry of External Affairs, Govt. of India), Asian Association of Open Universities (AAOU),  Innovation Council of India and the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, - IIFT (Ministry of Commerce, Govt. of India). Major publications include “संयुक्त राष्ट्र हिंदी-फ्रासीसी कोश" (Hindi-French Bilingual Dictionary), Ministry of Education, Govt of India and four more books on Didactics of French Language, Translation and Interpretation, African Francophonie, and Mobility Studies, apart from numerous research publications as book chapters and articles in national and international journals. Was conferred upon the "Prix d’excellence de l’enseignement du français”– Award for Excellence in French Studies in 2023 by the Institut français en Inde –IFI, Embassy of France in India. I am honoured and privileged to lead Maharashtra State Skills University as its Founding Vice Chancellor. The university stand on the Principles of making Education the pathway to make students confident by imparting appropriate skills and knowledge that is the need of the industry and Society at large. It is envisaged that the University shall nurture talent who can contribute responsibly to the future Society. While Skills and Knowledge imparting remains the core focus for the University the educational Goal is to create persons of high moral and ethics. As stated by Swami Vivekananda “We want the education by which character is formed, strength of mind is increased, the intellect is expanded, and by which one can stand on one’s own feet” MSSU shall strive to create empowered youth who shall be provided hands on skilling, foundation skilling, upskilling , reskilling and building future skills acumen at all levels with multiple entry and exit options.
